body.x: Camelotech (CEO Jung Won-chul) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri, local time), and unveiled a specialized herbal medicine production automation system for traditional Korean medicine clinics and hospitals.

Since its establishment in 2020, Camelotech has been devoted to innovating the manufacturing, compounding, and prescribing methods of traditional herbal medicines in traditional Korean medicine. Camelotech’s HAP system automates virtually every step of the herbal medicine production process, from preparation and manufacturing to packaging and cleaning, with just one click, according to the company. Additionally, this system allows users to check the remaining herbal medicines in real-time and place orders online.

In traditional Korean medicine, treatment and prescription occur within hospitals, involving the compounding and manufacturing of herbal medications on-site. The HAP system aims to automate and streamline these manual processes, ultimately reducing the workload of traditional Korean medicine clinics.

In particular, existing herbal medicine manufacturing equipment is known to have a minimum boiling time of 200 minutes. After transferring to packaging equipment, it is cleansed to prepare herbal medicines for the next patient. In contrast, the HAP system can produce up to 40 sheets (2 boxes) in under 5 minutes, and its internal facilities can be automatically cleaned and sterilized, according to the explanation.

A Camelotech representative met at CES 2024 and said, “Our company aims to expand beyond traditional herbal medicine manufacturing into the market for creating customized medicines. We especially aim to enable personalized prescriptions for healthy functional foods that can be consumed,” and added, “Through this exhibition, we hope to gain insights into how to localize and approach the U.S. market actively.”

body.x: He continued, “The company’s vision is to expand globally, starting from Japan beyond the Korean market. Following CES, we plan to actively enhance the recognition of our solutions in the U.S. market,” explained the background of their participation in the exhibition.

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
